purpose: Authoritative-vendor delta for three previously discovery-queued manufacturing integrations. Promotes Siemens WinCC, MaintainX and Fiix CMMS to spec-verified only, corrects the Fiix protocol classification away from REST, and records least-privilege/data-value boundaries. No sandbox or tenant credentials were used and no writes are enabled.

patch.evidenceNote: Current Siemens documentation identifies SIMATIC WinCC/WinCC Unified as OPC UA server/client-capable SCADA/HMI products. OPC UA itself can read, write, subscribe and invoke functionality, and WinCC security configuration can permit anonymous/no-security modes in some variants. Manufacturing WFM therefore uses only customer-approved Browse/Read/Subscribe data behind the site edge, requires a named identity, approved certificate trust and signed/encrypted sessions, and does not enable Write, method calls or alarm/control operations. Exact WinCC variant/version capabilities must be discovered per site. No WinCC runtime was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: dedicated named OPC UA identity limited to customer-approved WinCC nodes
Browse, Read and Subscribe only; no Write, method invocation, alarm acknowledgement or process-control actions
customer-approved server/client certificates and endpoint trust with signed or signed-and-encrypted sessions
no anonymous or no-security production sessions
dataAvailableOrExpected: customer-published process and machine tags from the WinCC OPC UA information model
machine or line state and production counters where modelled by the customer project
alarms and condition/event context where the WinCC variant and publication configuration expose them
node hierarchy and semantic names that can assist mapping to sites, lines and work centres
historical or archived observations only where the deployed WinCC variant exposes them through an approved read surface
automationOpportunities: adjust labour-demand and redeployment recommendations from actual line/machine state without direct PLC access
trigger human review of staffing risks when downtime or alarms reduce executable production
reuse WinCC node hierarchy to accelerate site, line and work-centre mapping during implementation
correlate shift labour, overtime and paid-idle periods with production counters and downtime evidence
savingsHypotheses: reduce bespoke PLC integration by consuming an existing governed WinCC OPC UA projection
reduce paid idle time by aligning labour recommendations with actual equipment availability
reduce avoidable overtime by surfacing production recovery and constraint changes earlier
reduce implementation mapping effort by reusing the SCADA information model and node hierarchy
dataGaps: tag naming, engineering units, hierarchy and business semantics are customer/project specific
WinCC product generations and editions expose different capabilities and security configuration
SCADA does not normally provide authoritative worker, payroll, absence, skills or agency-labour truth
alarm or archived data availability must be proven per deployed variant rather than inferred from OPC UA support
constraintsRisks: OPC UA is bidirectional and may expose writes/methods; WFM operation allowlists must remain read/subscription only
some WinCC configurations can permit anonymous or reduced-security OPC UA; those modes are not acceptable for production WFM
WinCC normally resides in protected plant networks, so the customer/site edge remains mandatory
version/variant differences require capability discovery and node-schema fingerprints before mapping is trusted
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing OPC UA edge adapter for a thin WinCC profile. On an authorised WinCC runtime, discover endpoint/version and approved namespace read-only, prove named-user/certificate authentication and Sign/SignAndEncrypt, snapshot the allowed node schema, test reconnect/subscription replay and source timestamps, and normalize representative machine-state/downtime/production observations before promotion beyond spec verification.

patch.evidenceNote: Current MaintainX documentation confirms a bearer-token REST API, updatedAt polling with pagination/deduplication, signed webhooks, external identifiers for cross-system identity, and a Reporting/Power BI API-key mode that cannot modify data. Webhook subscriptions themselves are configurable/mutative and therefore remain outside the normal WFM data-plane authority. MaintainX also documents region-specific OT connector endpoints and customer-side outbound-only industrial data paths, but those do not grant WFM direct plant-network authority. No MaintainX tenant was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: prefer a read-only Reporting/Power BI API key where its endpoint coverage is sufficient for the WFM workflow
otherwise use a dedicated bearer API key constrained to the minimum required organization/data scope
verify webhook timestamps/signatures and provision subscription configuration out-of-band rather than granting the runtime subscription-management authority
bind multi-organization and regional routing explicitly and do not reuse tokens across customer tenants
dataAvailableOrExpected: work orders and work-order status changes exposed through the REST API/webhooks
locations and parts including stable external identifiers where configured
work requests and other maintenance entities exposed by the customer's enabled API surface
change timestamps for incremental polling plus webhook occurrence metadata for event-driven reconciliation
automationOpportunities: turn planned/emergency maintenance demand into workforce requirements and qualified-worker recommendations
combine maintenance status changes with production schedules to reduce avoidable production/maintenance clashes
use external identifiers to reconcile assets/locations with ERP, MES and WFM records without duplicate master data
use signed webhooks plus updatedAt catch-up polling so missed events do not leave staffing decisions stale
correlate maintenance response, work-order timing and equipment availability with overtime and shift outcomes
savingsHypotheses: reduce emergency callout and overtime by exposing maintenance demand earlier to workforce planning
reduce avoidable downtime by matching maintenance work with available qualified labour and production windows
reduce integration reconciliation effort using stable external identifiers for assets, locations and parts
reduce polling load and latency by combining signed webhooks with incremental catch-up polling
dataGaps: authoritative employee contracts, payroll, absence and broad skills records normally remain in HCM/WFM/payroll systems
work-order labour standards and skill requirements depend on customer configuration
externalId is only supported on documented entity types and records a single external identifier per entity
available API data and organization scope depend on plan, key type and customer configuration
constraintsRisks: REST keys can expose mutative operations even though WFM remains read-only; prefer the documented non-modifying Reporting key where possible
webhook configuration endpoints create/update/delete subscriptions and remain management-plane operations
incremental polling must handle pagination, updatedAt overlap windows and deduplication by stable ID
regional and multi-organization routing must be pinned so data cannot cross a customer's intended boundary
OT connector telemetry may originate from protected plant networks; WFM must consume the approved cloud projection rather than gaining inbound plant access
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST/OpenAPI and signed-webhook adapters. In an authorised MaintainX environment, first prove a read-only Reporting key against the required asset/work-order/location endpoints; if insufficient, document the minimum dedicated REST-key scope. Validate pagination, updatedAt overlap/dedupe, webhook signature/replay handling, externalId reconciliation, region/org binding and representative read normalization before promotion beyond spec verification.

patch.evidenceNote: Fiix's current official API FAQ explicitly states that the Fiix API is not RESTful and is not SOAP. It is a cloud HTTPS/JSON API with Java and JavaScript SDKs and two request families: object requests and RPCs. API keys inherit both the associated user's permissions and CMMS-wide configuration, and the documented usage limit is 1,000 API calls per day per user licence. The previous generic REST classification was therefore incorrect; Manufacturing WFM now uses the existing vendor-thin SDK/custom-API path and keeps all object/RPC mutations disabled. No Fiix tenant was authenticated or queried.

requiredPermissions: dedicated Fiix API user/application keys with user-group/role permissions limited to the required read/find object operations
read-only access to only the required Work Order, Asset, Task and related maintenance objects
no create, change, remove or mutative RPC permissions
tenant subdomain and keys isolated per customer and kept at the executor boundary
dataAvailableOrExpected: other maintenance objects made available by the customer's Fiix API permissions
meter/asset-state context where the customer uses the documented Fiix API use cases
automationOpportunities: turn maintenance work-order demand into staffing and qualified-worker recommendations
correlate asset state and maintenance work with production disruption, emergency overtime and shift outcomes
schedule API synchronization within the documented daily call budget using change watermarks and customer-priority objects
reuse the vendor-thin custom API adapter rather than pretending Fiix follows REST semantics
savingsHypotheses: reduce emergency callout and overtime by exposing maintenance demand to workforce planning
reduce downtime by aligning maintenance work with qualified labour and production windows
reduce integration defects/support effort by modelling Fiix object/RPC semantics correctly instead of using a false REST abstraction
reduce API throttling incidents by planning synchronization around the documented licence-based daily call budget
dataGaps: API availability requires the Fiix Enterprise plan
worker contracts, payroll, absence and broad qualification truth normally remain outside Fiix
CMMS v5/v6 configuration changes object/action availability; v6 User API access is read-only while other object behaviour must be checked against the deployed account
exact object fields and relationships must be capability-discovered from the customer's current Fiix API reference/tenant
constraintsRisks: Fiix is not REST or SOAP; generic REST pagination/error assumptions must not be applied
API keys inherit the associated user's permissions and CMMS-wide configuration, so least privilege must be proved rather than inferred
object requests and RPCs can modify data; WFM must technically block create/change/remove and mutative RPC operations
the documented 1,000-calls-per-day-per-user-licence limit requires budgeted polling, backoff and prioritized synchronization
Fiix account version differences can change accessible objects/actions
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing vendor-thin SDK/custom-API profile rather than the REST adapter. In an authorised Fiix Enterprise tenant, discover the deployed API/account version and permitted object/RPC catalogue, prove a dedicated read-only user's Find/read behavior on Work Orders, Assets and Tasks, verify rate-budget handling and error semantics, fingerprint representative schemas and normalize read results before promotion beyond spec verification.
